title: Operating Systems MCQ Drill
heading: MCQ Drill
lede: Pick an answer and see at once whether it is right. A wrong pick shows the correct choice, and the solved bank adds the explanation and slide reference.
foot: Questions and answer keys are copied from your three PDFs as printed. Essay questions are left out. Progress is saved in this browser only.

questions.text: What is an operating system?
options: interface between the hardware and application programs
collection of programs that manages hardware resources
system service provider to the application programs
questions.why: Slide Ch1.5 & Ch1.9 define the OS as an intermediary between user/applications and hardware, allocating resources and managing hardware execution.

questions.text: How does the software trigger an interrupt?
options: Sending signals to CPU through bus
Executing a special operation called system call
Executing a special program called system program
Executing a special program called interrupt trigger program
questions.why: Slide Ch1.12 & Ch1.38 state that a trap or exception is a software-generated interrupt triggered by executing a system call (or error).

questions.text: How does the Hardware trigger an interrupt?
options: Sending signals to CPU through a system bus
Executing a special program called interrupt program
Executing a special program called system program
Executing a special operation called system call
questions.why: Hardware triggers interrupts by sending an electrical signal to the CPU via the system bus (Ch1 Slide 12, 14, 16).

questions.text: What is a trap/exception?
options: hardware generated interrupt caused by an error
software generated interrupt caused by an error
user generated interrupt caused by an error
questions.why: Slide Ch1.12 explicitly defines: “A trap or exception is a software-generated interrupt caused either by an error or a user request.”

questions.text: Division by zero, accessing a protected or non existent memory address, or attempting to execute a privileged instruction from user mode are all categorized as ......
questions.why: Runtime CPU execution errors (like zero division or illegal memory access) generate software exceptions (traps) per Ch1 Slide 12 & 37.

questions.text: What is an ISR?
questions.why: Slide Ch1.12 states: “Interrupt transfers control to the interrupt service routine”.

questions.text: What is an interrupt vector?
options: It is an address that is indexed to an interrupt handler
It is a unique device number that is indexed by an address
It is a unique identity given to an interrupt
questions.why: Slide Ch1.12 defines the interrupt vector as containing the addresses of all the service routines indexed by interrupt request.

questions.text: The interrupt vector contains ......
options: the memory addresses of specialized interrupt handlers
questions.why: Slide Ch1.12 states: “the interrupt vector, which contains the addresses of all the service routines”.

questions.text: Which operation is performed by an interrupt handler?
options: Saving the current state of the system
Loading the interrupt handling code and executing it
Once done handling, bringing back the system to the original state it was before the interrupt occurred
questions.why: Slides Ch1.13 & Ch1.14 depict saving CPU state/registers, processing data in the handler, and resuming the interrupted task.

questions.text: The ...... determines the cause of the interrupt, performs the necessary processing and executes a return from the interrupt instruction to return the CPU to the execution state prior to the interrupt.
questions.why: Slide Ch1.14 flow diagram shows: “interrupt handler processes data, returns from interrupt” to resume CPU processing.

questions.text: The hardware mechanism that allows a device to notify the CPU is called ......
questions.why: Slide Ch1.16 explicitly states: “Device controller informs CPU that it has finished its operation by causing an interrupt.”

questions.text: In an interrupt driven input/output ......
options: the CPU uses polling to watch the control bit constantly, looping to see if a device is ready
the CPU writes one data byte to the data register and sets a bit in control register to show that a byte is available
the CPU receives an interrupt when the device is ready for the next byte
the CPU runs a user written code and does accordingly
questions.why: Slide Ch1.14 & Ch1.16 demonstrate that in interrupt-driven I/O, the CPU continues executing until notified by an I/O completion interrupt signal.

questions.text: If one or more devices use a common set of wires to communicate with the computer system, the connection is called ......
questions.why: Slide Ch1.11 shows CPUs and device controllers connecting through a “common bus providing access to shared memory”.

questions.text: A ...... is a collection of electronics that can operate a port, a bus, or a device.
questions.why: Slide Ch1.16 & Ch1.22 specify that each device controller (electronic chip/board) is in charge of a particular device/bus type.

questions.text: DMA is used for ......
options: High speed devices (disks and communications network)
questions.why: Slide Ch1.26 states verbatim: “Used for high-speed I/O devices able to transmit information at close to memory speeds”.

questions.text: For large data transfers, ...... is used.
questions.why: Slide Ch1.26 states DMA transfers blocks of data directly to memory generating only one interrupt per block instead of per byte.

questions.text: The ...... presents a uniform device-access interface to the I/O subsystem, much as system calls provide a standard interface between the application and the operating system.
questions.why: Slide Ch1.24 states: “Device Driver for each device controller... Provides uniform interface between controller and kernel”.

questions.text: A non blocking system call ......
options: halts the execution of the application for an extended time
does not halt the execution of the application
questions.why: Slide Ch1.17 & Ch1.18 explain asynchronous/non-blocking I/O returns control to the user program without waiting for I/O completion.

questions.text: An asynchronous call ......
options: returns immediately, without waiting for the I/O to complete
does not return immediately and waits for the I/O to complete
questions.why: Slide Ch1.18 defines asynchronous mode: “After I/O starts, control returns to user program without waiting for I/O completion.”

questions.text: A process is moved to wait queue when I/O request is made with ......
questions.why: Slide Ch1.18 describes synchronous/blocking I/O where the wait instruction idles the process/CPU until I/O completion.

questions.text: The device-status table contains ......
questions.why: Slide Ch1.18 explicitly states: “Device-status table contains entry for each I/O device indicating its type, address, and state”.

questions.text: Which hardware triggers some operation after certain programmed count?
questions.why: Slide Ch1.45 describes the hardware Timer set to interrupt after a time period by decrementing a counter to zero.

questions.text: Caching ......
options: holds a copy of the data
holds the only copy of the data
questions.why: Slide Ch1.24 & Ch1.47 define caching as copying information into faster storage temporarily (holding a temporary copy).

questions.text: Caching is ...... spooling.
questions.why: Slide Ch1.47 distinguishes buffering (temporary storage), caching (faster storage copy), and spooling (overlapping output of one job with input of another).

questions.text: Spooling ......
options: holds a copy of the data
holds the only copy of the data
questions.why: Slide Ch1.47 defines spooling as “the overlapping of output of one job with input of other jobs” (spooling printer jobs).

questions.text: Which buffer holds the output for a device?
questions.why: Slide Ch1.47 identifies spooling as the buffer mechanism managing overlapping output for devices.

questions.text: A memory buffer used to accommodate a speed differential is called ......
questions.why: Slide Ch1.25 & Ch1.47 explain buffering/caching as storing data in faster memory to accommodate speed differentials between components.

questions.text: CPU fetches the instruction from memory according to the value of ......
questions.why: Slide Ch1.38 defines the program counter as specifying the location of the next instruction to execute.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not a secondary storage?
questions.why: Slide Ch1.21 & Ch1.23 categorize RAM (DRAM) as volatile Main Memory (primary storage), whereas secondary storage comprises HDDs, SSDs, etc.

questions.text: Virtual memory uses disk space as an extension of ......
questions.why: Slide Ch1.34 states virtual memory allows execution of processes not completely in physical main memory.

questions.text: Virtual memory allows ......
options: execution of a process that may not be completely in memory
a program to be smaller than the physical memory
a program to be larger than the secondary storage
execution of a process without being in physical memory
questions.why: Slide Ch1.34 explicitly states: “Virtual memory allows execution of processes not completely in memory”.

questions.text: In ...... information is recorded magnetically on platters.
questions.why: Slide Ch1.22 defines HDDs as: “rigid metal or glass platters covered with magnetic recording material”.

questions.text: ...... tend to represent a major bottleneck in system performance.
questions.why: Slide Ch1.43 states: “Entire speed of computer operation hinges on disk subsystem and its algorithms” due to mechanical seek latency.

questions.text: Some directory information is kept in main memory or cache to ......
options: increase free space in secondary storage
decrease free space in secondary storage
questions.why: Slide Ch1.25 & Ch1.47 note that caching information in faster storage speeds up access compared to disk fetching.

questions.text: Data cannot be written to secondary storage unless written within a ......
questions.why: Slide Ch1.42 defines a file as the logical storage unit provided by the OS to abstract physical storage media.

questions.text: A file is a/an ...... data type.
questions.why: Slide Ch1.42 states: “OS provides uniform, logical view of information storage. Abstracts physical properties to logical storage unit - file”.

questions.text: The address of the next instruction to be executed by the current process is provided by the ......
questions.why: Slide Ch1.38 defines: “Single-threaded process has one program counter specifying location of next instruction to execute”.

questions.text: A single thread of control allows the process to perform ......
options: only one task at a time
only two tasks at a time
questions.why: Slide Ch1.38 states a single-threaded process executes instructions sequentially, one at a time.

questions.text: What is the objective of multiprogramming?
options: Have a process running at all time
Have multiple programs waiting in a queue ready to run
questions.why: Slide Ch1.33 states multiprogramming organizes jobs so the CPU always has one to execute, preventing idle CPU time.

questions.text: In a multiprogramming environment ......
options: the processor executes more than one process at a time
the programs are developed by more than one person
more than one process resides in the memory
a single user can execute many programs at the same time
questions.why: Slide Ch1.33 & Ch1.35 explicitly state: “A subset of total jobs in system is kept in memory” (shown in memory layout slide 35).

questions.text: With ...... only one process can execute at a time; meanwhile all other process are waiting for the processor. With ...... more than one process can be running simultaneously each on a different processor.
questions.why: Slides Ch1.28 & Ch1.33 contrast uniprocessor multiprogramming (interleaved execution) with multiprocessing (true simultaneous execution on multiple CPUs).

questions.text: A process can be ......
questions.why: Slide Ch1.38 notes that processes can be single-threaded (one program counter) or multi-threaded (one program counter per thread).

questions.text: Which one of the following is not shared by threads?
questions.why: Slide Ch1.38 states each thread has its own program counter and stack to maintain its distinct execution state.

questions.text: A process having multiple threads of control implies ......
options: it can do more than one task at a time
it can do only one task at a time, but much faster
it has to use only one thread per process
questions.why: Slide Ch1.38 explains multithreading enables a process to perform multiple tasks concurrently across different threads.

questions.text: For system protection, a process should access ......
options: only those resources for which it has authorization
few resources but authorization is not required
questions.why: Slide Ch1.48 defines Protection as controlling access of processes/users to resources defined by the OS using authorization/User IDs.

questions.text: What is the main objective of protection?
options: Ensure all objects are protected individually
Objects have different priority and thus different levels of protection
Ensure that each object is accessed correctly and only by allowed processes
questions.why: Slide Ch1.48 states protection mechanisms control resource access and enforce user access control policies.

questions.text: Reliability of files can be increased by ......
options: keeping the files safely in the memory
making a different partition for the files
by keeping them in external storage
by keeping duplicate copies of the file
questions.why: Slide Ch1.41 lists “Backup files onto stable (non-volatile) storage media” (duplicate copies) under file management activities.

questions.text: What is used to protect network from outside internet access?
options: Firewall to separate trusted and untrusted network
Deny users access to websites which can potentially cause security leak
questions.why: Slide Ch1.53 & Ch1.63 explicitly mention firewalls used to protect computers/networks from Internet attacks.

questions.text: The machine containing the files is the ...... and the machine wanting to access the files is the ......
questions.why: Slide Ch1.56 defines client-server computing: “File-server system provides interface for clients to store and retrieve files”.

questions.text: What are the characteristics of processor in distributed system?
options: They vary in size and function
They are same in size and function
They are manufactured with single purpose
questions.why: Slide Ch1.55 defines distributed systems as a collection of “separate, possibly heterogeneous, systems networked together”.

questions.text: In real time operating system ......
options: process scheduling can be done only once
all processes have the same priority
a task must be serviced by its deadline period
questions.why: Slide Ch1.64 defines RTOS: “Real-time OS has well-defined fixed time constraints. Processing must be done within constraint”.

questions.text: In a real time system the computer results ......
options: must be produced within a specific deadline period
may be produced at any time
questions.why: Slide Ch1.64 states: “Correct operation only if constraints met” (deadlines strictly enforced).

questions.text: What is the main function of the command interpreter?
options: to provide the interface between the API and application program
to handle the files in the operating system
to get and execute the next user-specified command
questions.why: Slide Ch2a.8 states: “Command Line interpreter... Primarily fetches a command from user and executes it”.

questions.text: Which one of the following errors will be handle by the operating system?
questions.why: Slide Ch2a.6 states Error Detection handles hardware (CPU/memory), I/O device (printer/power), and network errors.

questions.text: The usual effect of abnormal termination of a program is ......
questions.why: Slide Ch2a.21 lists process control system calls: “Dump memory if error” for post-mortem debugging.

questions.text: To access the services of the operating system, the interface is provided by the ......
questions.why: Slide Ch2a.13 states: “System Calls: Programming interface to the services provided by the OS”.

questions.text: Whenever a process needs I/O to or from a disk it issues a ......
options: system call to the operating system
questions.why: Slide Ch2a.14 & Ch2a.22 state processes request disk reading/writing via file management system calls (open, read, write).

questions.text: By using the specific system call, we can ......
questions.why: Slide Ch2a.22 lists file management calls: open, close, read, write, reposition, create, delete.

questions.text: For processes to request access to file contents, they need ......
options: to implement the open and close system calls
questions.why: Slide Ch2a.14 & Ch2a.22 show file access requires opening the file first and closing it upon completion.

questions.text: Standard set of functions through which interacts with kernel is defined by ......
questions.why: Slide Ch2a.16 states standard C libraries provide the system-call interface for programs to interact with the kernel.

questions.text: In Unix, which system call creates the new process?
questions.why: Slide Ch2a.25 & Ch2a.27 state Unix process creation uses the `fork()` system call.

questions.text: Which system call can be used by a parent process to determine the termination of child process?
questions.why: Slide Ch2a.25 & Ch2a.27 state parent shell/process calls `wait()` (`WaitForSingleObject()` in Windows) to wait for child termination.

questions.text: A parent process calling ...... system call will be suspended until children processes terminate.
questions.why: Slide Ch2a.27 explicitly states: “Shell waits for process to terminate” using the `wait()` system call.

questions.text: Which of the following system calls transforms executable binary file into a process?
questions.why: Slide Ch2a.27 states: “Executes exec() to load program into process”.

questions.text: What is Interprocess communication?
options: allows processes to communicate and synchronize their actions when using the same address space
allows processes to communicate and synchronize their actions
allows the processes to only synchronize their actions without communication
questions.why: Slide Ch2a.6 & Ch2a.23 state communications allow processes to exchange info and synchronize via shared memory or message passing across address spaces.

questions.text: Message passing system allows processes to ......
options: communicate with each other without sharing the same address space
communicate with one another by resorting to shared data
name the recipient or sender of the message
questions.why: Slide Ch2a.6 notes message passing moves packets via OS between separate address spaces (unlike shared memory).

questions.text: Which of the following two operations are provided by the IPC facility?
questions.why: Slide Ch2a.23 explicitly lists message passing operations: “send, receive messages if message passing model”.

questions.text: Processes on the remote systems are identified by ......
questions.why: Slide Ch2a.23 states remote message passing requires specifying the host name or process name/identifier.

questions.text: Which file is a sequence of bytes organized into blocks understandable by the system’s linker?
questions.why: Slide Ch2a.32 & Ch2a.33 define relocatable object files (`.o`) compiled from source code and processed by the linker into an executable binary.

questions.text: Operating systems provide an environment for ______.
options: execution of programs and services to programs and users

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a type of user interface?
Which OS service loads a program into memory, runs it, and ends its execution normally or abnormally?
A running program that needs to read from a file or a device uses which OS service?
Which of the following is a file-system manipulation service?
options: Creating and deleting files and directories

questions.text: Processes may exchange information on the same computer or over a network using the ______ service.
Communications between processes may be via ______.
In message passing, the packets are moved by ______.
Which service means the OS must be constantly aware of possible errors in the CPU, memory, I/O devices and user programs?
Which OS function ensures efficient operation of the system itself through resource sharing?
When multiple users or jobs run concurrently, resources such as CPU cycles, main memory, file storage and I/O devices must be ______.
Which service keeps track of which users use how much and what kinds of computer resources?
Ensuring that all access to system resources is controlled is called ______.
Security of the system from outsiders requires ______.
What is the main function of the command interpreter?
options: To provide the interface between the API and the application program
To handle the files in the operating system
To get and execute the next user-specified command

questions.text: A command-line interface (CLI) allows ______.
Multiple flavors of command-line interpreters are called ______.
If shell commands are just names of programs, then adding new features ______.
Bourne shell is an example of a ______.
The GUI was invented at ______.
In a GUI, icons represent ______.
The Apple Mac OS X GUI is called ______.
Microsoft Windows is a GUI with a CLI ______ shell.
Which are GUI interfaces available on UNIX and Linux?
Touchscreen interfaces are based on ______.
System calls are ______.
options: the programming interface to the services provided by the OS

questions.text: System calls are typically written in ______.
Programs mostly access system calls through ______.
Which are the three most common APIs?
The POSIX API is used by ______.
options: virtually all versions of UNIX, Linux and Mac OS X

questions.text: In the C library example, the printf() library call calls the ______ system call.
The system-call interface maintains a table that is indexed according to ______.
options: the number associated with each system call

questions.text: The caller of a system call needs to know ______.
options: nothing about how it is implemented, just obey the API
how the system call is implemented

questions.text: Most details of the OS interface are hidden from the programmer by the ______.
options: API (managed by the run-time support library)

questions.text: To access the services of the operating system, the interface is provided by the ______.
Which is NOT one of the three general methods used to pass parameters to the OS?
options: Store the parameters in a block (table) in memory and pass its address in a register
Push the parameters onto the stack

questions.text: Which parameter-passing method is the simplest?
Which OS take the approach of storing parameters in a block (table) in memory and passing its address in a register?
Which parameter-passing methods do NOT limit the number or length of parameters?
create process, terminate process, load, execute, wait event and allocate memory are system calls of which type?
open, close, read, write, reposition and get/set file attributes are ______ system calls.
request device, release device and logically attach or detach devices are ______ system calls.
get time or date, set time or date and get system data are ______ system calls.
Create/delete communication connection and send/receive messages are ______ system calls.
Get and set permissions and allow or deny user access are ______ system calls.
In the shared-memory model of communication, system calls are used to ______.
options: create and gain access to memory regions

questions.text: The Arduino is an example of a system that is ______.
In the Arduino example, programs (sketches) are loaded via USB into ______ by the boot loader.
In FreeBSD, the shell executes the ______ system call to create a process.
In FreeBSD, the shell then executes ______ to load a program into the process.
In FreeBSD, a process exits with code = 0 meaning ______.
In FreeBSD, a process that exits with code > 0 means ______.
A parent process calling the ______ system call will be suspended until its child processes terminate.
System programs provide ______.
options: a convenient environment for program development and execution

questions.text: Most users' view of the operating system is defined by ______.
Which system program categories are listed in the chapter?
options: File manipulation, status information, programming language support, program loading and execution, communications, background services, application programs

questions.text: A registry is used to ______.
Background services that launch at boot time are also known as ______.
Background services run in ______.
Application programs are ______.
options: not typically considered part of the OS

questions.text: Source code is compiled into ______ files designed to be loaded into any physical memory location.
The ______ combines object files into a single binary executable file and also brings in libraries.
The ______ brings the program from secondary storage into memory to be executed.
Relocation ______.
options: assigns final addresses to program parts and adjusts code and data to match

questions.text: Dynamically linked libraries (DLLs in Windows) are ______.
options: loaded as needed and shared by all that use the same version

questions.text: Why are applications usually operating system specific?
options: Each OS provides its own unique system calls, file formats, etc.

questions.text: Which of the following allows an app to run on multiple operating systems?
options: Writing it in an interpreted language like Python
Compiling it once for Windows only

questions.text: The Application Binary Interface (ABI) is ______.
options: the architecture equivalent of API, defining how binary code components interface on a given OS and architecture

questions.text: An operating system is a program that acts as an intermediary between ______.
options: a user and the computer hardware

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a goal of an operating system?
options: Execute user programs and make solving user problems easier
Make the computer system convenient to use

questions.text: The one program running at all times on the computer is the ______.
A program that ships with the operating system but is not part of the kernel is called a ______.
Middleware is ______.
options: a hardware component between CPU and memory
a set of software frameworks providing additional services to application developers
the part of the kernel that handles interrupts

questions.text: A computer system can be divided into four components. Which is NOT one of them?
The operating system is considered a ______ and control program.
What is a bootstrap program?
options: The first code executed when the computer system is started
A program that only restarts the system
A simple program like any other program

questions.text: The bootstrap program initializes all aspects of the system, from CPU registers to device controllers and memory contents, and then ______.
options: starts the operating system (loads the kernel)

questions.text: Which of the following contains the addresses of all the interrupt service routines?
A trap (exception) is ______.
options: a hardware interrupt from a device
a software-generated interrupt caused by an error or a user request

questions.text: Modern operating systems are ______.
When an interrupt occurs, the operating system preserves the state of the CPU by storing ______.
options: the registers and the program counter

questions.text: A device controller informs the CPU that it has finished its operation by ______.
The ______ presents a uniform device-access interface between the device controller and the kernel.
Each device controller has a local ______.
A buffer is a ______.
options: temporary area for data while it is being transferred

questions.text: Direct Memory Access (DMA) is used for high-speed I/O devices. How many interrupts are generated?
The only large storage medium that the CPU can access directly is ______.
Main memory is typically ______.
options: volatile and implemented as magnetic disk

questions.text: Which storage is the fastest in the storage hierarchy?
Moving down the storage hierarchy (registers to tape), the capacity ______ and the speed ______.
Caching means ______.
options: copying information into a faster storage system temporarily

questions.text: What type of memory stores data in a swap file on a hard drive?
Which of the following is nonvolatile memory (NVM) that is faster than a hard disk?
One kilobyte (KB) equals ______.
A byte consists of ______ bits.
In a hard disk drive, the disk surface is logically divided into ______.
options: tracks, which are subdivided into sectors
sectors, which are subdivided into tracks

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of multiprocessor systems?
In ______ multiprocessing, each processor performs all tasks.
In ______ multiprocessing, each processor is assigned a specific task.
Asymmetric clustering has ______.
Multiprocessor systems are also known as ______.
What is the objective of multiprogramming?
options: Have a process running at all times so the CPU is always busy

questions.text: In multiprogramming, when a job has to wait (for I/O for example), the OS ______.
Multitasking (timesharing) allows ______.
options: multiple users to share a single device only
the CPU to switch between jobs so frequently that users can interact with each job while it runs
devices to run without an OS
only one process at a time

questions.text: In a time-sharing system, response time should be ______.
If several jobs are ready to run at the same time, the system must perform ______.
If processes don't fit in memory, ______ moves them in and out of memory to run.
Dual-mode operation allows the OS to ______.
options: protect itself and other system components

questions.text: When kernel code is executing, the mode bit is ______.
Privileged instructions can be executed only in ______.
A system call changes the mode to ______, and the return from the call resets it to ______.
The timer is used to ______.
options: prevent an infinite loop or a process hogging resources

questions.text: A process is ______.
options: a passive entity stored on disk
a program in execution (an active entity)

questions.text: A single-threaded process has ______.
Which is NOT a process-management activity of the OS?
Which of the following is an activity of mass-storage management?
The overlapping of the output of one job with the input of other jobs is called ______.
______ is any mechanism for controlling the access of processes or users to resources defined by the OS.
______ allows a user to change to an effective ID with more rights.
In a multiprocessor environment, ______ ensures that all CPUs have the most recent value in their cache.
The search performance of a balanced binary search tree is ______.
A bitmap is ______.
options: a string of n binary digits representing the status of n items

questions.text: Which computing environment places rigid time requirements on the operation of a processor or the flow of data?
In a real-time OS, correct operation occurs ______.
options: only if the time constraints are met

questions.text: Which operating system runs on a server and provides the capability to manage data, users, groups, etc.?
Which operating system uses multiple central processors to serve multiple real-time applications and multiple users?
Which of the following is NOT a type of operating system?
In ______ computing, there is no distinction between clients and servers; all nodes are peers.
Which of the following is an example of peer-to-peer computing?
options: Voice over IP such as Skype
A database server with thin clients

questions.text: In client-server computing, a ______ provides an interface for clients to store and retrieve files.
Emulation is used when ______.
options: the source CPU type differs from the target CPU type

questions.text: The component that provides virtualization services is called the ______.
Which cloud service model provides servers or storage over the Internet?
A cloud that is run by a company for the company's own use is a ______ cloud.
Mobile operating system leaders are ______.
The GNU Public License (GPL) was started by the ______.
Which of the following is an example of free and open-source operating systems?
In the abstract view of a computer, the operating system sits between ______.
options: the user and the application programs
the application programs and the computer hardware
